name: tacli-promo
_stage: Tiles are 1024x768 because that is what `tacli launch --res 1024x768` gives,
so a real clip drops into a tile 1:1 with no letterboxing (ta-capture rule 4).
The 64px gap is the desktop showing between windows — it is what makes the
wide shot read as 'a desktop full of games' rather than one big texture.
_camera: cols = how many window columns fit across the frame, interpolated in log
space. Centre (512,384) is hero 1's middle; (1056,800) the 2x2 block's.
The camera is FROZEN whenever text is being typed: 0-7.47s for hero 1, and
again from 10.5s (once the 2x2 framing has settled) through heroes 2-4.
Any zoom at all while text is on screen makes the glyphs crawl — the tile is
continuously resampled. Measured on the prompt region, temporal 2nd
difference: slow push 7.453, frozen 0.000. Do not add a 'subtle' push here.
_windows: The four hero windows. Each opens as a terminal, types its command, prints
output, then cross-fades into the game in the SAME rect — that is beat 2.
`clip` is the clip id used by --backend clip; `variant` only colours the
The map names and unit counts in `output` are REAL — read back from
`tacli scenario expand <name>` on 2026-09-10. The surrounding line format is
still a placeholder: capture a real `scenario load` transcript and match it.
_fill: The grid behind the heroes. Each cell gets a random clip and a random time
offset so no two tiles are in step. Range covers the cols=44 wide shot with
reveal.not_before is the hard gate that keeps beats 1-4 honest: until 22.0s
the desktop holds exactly the scripted windows (one, then four), so no
neighbour creeps into frame. At 22.0 the first ring fades up over `wave`
seconds — the desktop filling is a deliberate shot. Every outer ring is
already open `lead` seconds before the camera reaches it, so nothing pops
on screen. The times come from the camera path, so retiming the pull-back
retimes the reveal with no hand-edited open times.
_captions: The Card treatment: full-frame typographic cards, chosen from the five
prototype cuts on 2026-09-10. Claims are checked in the ta-video-montage
skill's table. Captions wrap and shrink to fit, so a long line is safe.
Beat 1's card sits AFTER the terminal flips to the game (4.6s, not 1.2s):
over the terminal it covered the command and the lines it printed.

captions.sub: no menu, no map setup, no clicking
edit it, commit it, re-run it
or as many as the machine will hold
